summary: Recurring 503 waves after tenant ephemeral connection surge; runtime kernel fallback and crashloops
description:
Issue summary:
Starting 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC FluentDocs reported repeated waves of 503/502 responses for a subset of tenant traffic. Errors correlate with short spikes of ephemeral TCP connections from the tenant (~1-2s lifespan) at ~1.2k req/s sustained for ~30s. API gateway logs show large numbers of connections in CLOSE_WAIT and many request contexts timed out with upstream response 503.

Impact:
- Customer SLA impact: multiple failed calls for streaming and non-streaming generation; estimated 8% request failure rate during each wave.
- Affected workloads: both streaming chat and batch generation; latency for successful requests increased by ~300-600ms.

Environment:
- Tenant: FluentDocs (dedicated pool)
- Region: prod-us-west (us-west-2)
- Models: gpt-medium-v1, gpt-large-v1
- Serving runtime version: v2.14.0-rc3
- Gateway version: apigw 1.9.2

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Tenant bursts ephemeral connections (short lived) from many client hosts.
2) API gateway connection pools hit high churn; many sockets rotated and short-lived TLS sessions.
3) Requests are routed to serving runtime; KV-prefetch and batching subsystems see cache thrash.
4) Some runtime workers hit kernel fallback paths (quantized kernel selection) and then exit with SIGABRT or OOM_kill under concurrent GC/alloc pressure.
5) Upstream exits produce 502/503 to client; gateway retries amplify if backend restart is slow.

Observed behavior:
- Gateway logs: repeated 502/503 with upstream "connection reset" and "no healthy upstream" messages.
- Runtime logs: repeated stack traces referencing 'kernel_select::fallback', 'kv_cache_miss_spike', 'prefetch_throttle::panic', and '/usr/bin/runtime: killed by SIGABRT'.
- Metrics: sudden spike in runtime process restarts (+150%), increase in apigw 502/503 rate from 0.2% to 8% for the tenant window.

Expected behavior:
- API gateway should shed load gracefully and route to warm fallbacks without causing widespread runtime crashloops.
- Runtime should avoid selecting unstable kernel fallback under high short-lived concurrency and instead throttle or queue.

Logs & traces (snippets):
- apigw: "conn_churn: pool_open=1200 pool_close=1187; handler_timeout=300ms; upstream_error=502; upstream_msg=connection reset by peer"
- runtime: "[2026-03-10T09:12:31Z] ERROR kernel_select: fallback triggered for model=gpt-large-v1; cpu_kernels_unavailable=2; nvlib_version=2.3.1"
- runtime: "/usr/bin/runtime[pid:23412]: abort() at kernel_runner.cc:412; reason=alloc_failure"

Mitigation applied:
- Support placed tenant on a temporary rate limiter (burst window 400 req/s) and enabled gateway keepalive-extension to favor reuse of TLS sessions.
- Scaled up dedicated serving pool by 6 instances (hot-add) to reduce per-worker load.
- Eng routed traffic to older stable runtime (v2.13.4) for the tenant as an emergency rollback.

Current hypothesis:
1) Short-lived connection surge causes apigw keepalive pool churn and SNI/TLS renegotiation amplification which increases per-request CPU and memory overhead.
2) Runtime kernel selector under v2.14.0-rc3 attempts fallback kernels under resource pressure which are less tested and can OOM or abort under high concurrency.
3) Combined effect leads to noisy neighbor overload inside the dedicated pool and runtime crashloops producing 502/503 amplification.

Next steps (investigation/engineering):
- SRE to capture end-to-end pcap for next burst window and correlate TLS session lifetimes with apigw process metrics.
- Runtime team to add guardrails in kernel selector: avoid fallback when process memory >75% and instead return 429 / queue.
- Product to consider permanent keepalive/burst controls for dedicated customers to limit connection churn.

Workaround/Resolution (temporary):
- Tenant remains on rate-limiter for ephemeral connections and routed to stable runtime. No full fix yet.

Notes:
- Related to but distinct from SUP-51234 (apigw saturation) and SUP-68410 (autoscaler warmup 503s); this ticket centers on kernel fallback crashloops induced by connection churn.

[2026-03-10 11:45 UTC] Diego Kim (SRE): Observed huge spike in TCP open/close rates. Confirmed apigw connection churn. Increased gateway keepalive pool and applied temporary tenant qps cap. Requested runtime logs from Eng.

[2026-03-10 12:30 UTC] Marcelo Ruiz (Runtime Eng): Found repeated aborts in kernel selector on v2.14.0-rc3 when concurrent alloc > 64GB. Rolling the tenant to v2.13.4 reduced restarts immediately. Opening PR to add memory-threshold guard.

[2026-03-11 09:20 UTC] Customer (FluentDocs): Confirmed errors dropped after rollback and rate limiting. They've requested timeline for permanent fix and whether dedicated pool can get kernel selector patch.

[2026-03-12 08:15 UTC] Marcelo Ruiz (Runtime Eng): PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321. Plan: backport guard to stable branch and prepare hotfix release v2.14.0-hotfix1. ETA for hotfix in staging 2026-03-14.
[2026-03-12 14:40 UTC] Aisha Patel (Support): Updated customer that hotfix is in progress and that we will schedule a maintenance window for dedicated pool patching. Keeping ticket In Progress.
resolution: workaround: tenant rate-limited and rolled back to v2.13.4; hotfix PR submitted; pending scheduled patch rollout
notes: This ticket should be monitored during the next tenant-burst window. Consider adding synthetic test for short-lived connection surges in CI for dedicated pools.
